findings.title: [단독] 다크웹에 '한전 개인정보·입찰자료 확보' 주장…전자조달시스템 SRM 관련 가능성 조사 필요
findings.summary_md: DailySecu reported a DarkForums post dated November 19 and attributed to the account Noiem, claiming 592,585 external user records, 95,054 supplier records, 401,951 bid price records and 26,859 sole-contract records from KEPCO. The listed supplier, bid and contract material overlaps the work handled by KEPCO's electronic procurement system at srm.kepco.net, but the post named no source system or intrusion path. The report said the data's authenticity, overlap with prior leaks and actual transfer outside KEPCO were unverified.

findings.title: 다크웹서 "한전 이용자 정보 확보" 게시물 등장
findings.summary_md: ZDNet Korea reported on the same DarkForums post, noting claims of 592,585 external user records and roughly 950,000 supplier records alongside bid and contract files. It said the data categories match SRM functions but that no source system was identified, so an SRM compromise could not be confirmed at that point. The article also recalled an October KEPCO leak that grew from about 24,000 employees to 35,528 people, including retirees and contractor staff, with coded facial recognition data for 400 employees.

findings.title: KEPCO Hack Exposes Data of 1.52 Million Users, Raising Grid Concerns
findings.summary_md: Seoul Economic Daily reported that KEPCO confirmed on November 20 the exposure of 12 data categories for 650,487 KEPCO ON customers, including resident and foreign registration numbers, bank and card details, and billing records, representing 7.1% of the platform's 9.2 million users. It reported 426,827 procurement representatives and 442,934 KEPCO and corporate employees affected through SRM, for 1,520,248 people in total. The article raised concern that SRM holds procurement records for power grid construction projects and that facility locations or equipment details could be exposed beyond the personal data.

findings.title: 한전, 고객 등 개인정보 152만여건 유출…주민·계좌번호 포함(종합)
findings.summary_md: Yonhap reported KEPCO's confirmation that 650,487 KEPCO ON users and 869,761 SRM users were affected, with 426,827 corporate representatives and 442,934 KEPCO and company employees in the latter group. It said the company treated the entire SRM user base as affected because individual exposure could not be determined, notified the Personal Information Protection Commission, and opened an investigation with the National Intelligence Service and the climate ministry's cyber safety center. KEPCO attributed the intrusion to an external attacker and cited increasingly sophisticated attacks using technologies such as AI without giving an access method.

findings.title: KEPCO reports another massive data breach
findings.summary_md: The Korea Times reported that KEPCO detected the intrusion on November 20, blocked external IP access and suspended the two systems, then notified affected people and worked with the National Intelligence Service and outside experts. It listed names, resident registration numbers, bank account details, credit card information and billing records for KEPCO ON users, alongside names, phone numbers and email addresses for 426,827 corporate representatives and names, affiliations and contact details for 442,934 employees. The report noted this was a second breach a month after a separate leak affecting 35,528 people.

findings.title: [단독 후속] 데일리시큐 19일 최초 보도한 한국전력 해킹, 152만 명 개인정보 유출로 확인…다크웹 게시물과 DB 유통 가능성 조사해야
findings.summary_md: DailySecu linked its November 19 report to KEPCO's November 22 confirmation of 1,520,248 affected records and said the earlier post by Noiem had also claimed military and government supplier data, with the whole set labeled as a 560M CSV. It stressed that the actor's claims about data volume, provenance and onward distribution were unverified and that neither KEPCO's announcement nor the regulator statement addressed the dark web posting. The article called for checking whether SRM or linked systems show abnormal queries or bulk exports and whether the material overlaps older leaks.

findings.title: 한전, 개인정보 유출 1만1천명 추가…퇴직자·협력사 직원 포함
findings.summary_md: Yonhap reported that an earlier KEPCO leak had grown from about 24,000 employees to 35,528 people after investigators found roughly 11,000 additional records belonging to retirees and 68 contractor staff. The exposed data included names, affiliations and phone numbers, plus coded facial recognition data from the headquarters access system for 400 current employees. KEPCO notified affected people, filed a report with the Personal Information Protection Commission and referred the case to police.
